rejected.title: Character, setting and events together
card: A narrative is a story. Its characters are the people or creatures in it. Its setting is the time and place. Its events are what happens.
These three work together. A writer can use the setting or an event to show what a character is like.
A storm or a sudden shock can put a character under pressure. How they react can show traits such as bravery, fear or kindness.
Example: a flood rises in the night. Kai wakes his little sister and carries her to the roof before he thinks of himself. This shows Kai is caring and brave.
rejected.remember: Setting and events can put a character under pressure, and how they react shows what they are like.

a.q: Zara's boat is hit by a sudden wave. She grips the wheel, calls calm orders to her crew and steers on. What does this event show about Zara?
opts: She is calm and takes the lead
She is careless and ignores danger
She is shy and avoids her crew
She is jealous and blames her crew
a.why: Zara's calm orders during a sudden wave show how she reacts under pressure, so the event reveals her as calm and a leader. Careless is tempting because she steers on, but she is giving orders to keep the crew safe, not ignoring the danger.
a.clue: Look at what Zara does when the wave hits.

b.q: Leo hears thunder as he walks home through a dark, empty park. He runs the whole way, glancing back at every shadow. Which statement best explains how the writer reveals Leo's character?
opts: The stormy, dark setting leads Leo to show he is fearful
The thunder tells readers that Leo is a strong runner
The park shows that Leo is lonely and wants friends
Leo's running shows that he is in a hurry to eat dinner
b.why: The passage never says Leo is afraid. Readers infer it from how he reacts to the dark, stormy park: he runs and keeps glancing back at shadows. The strong runner option is tempting because he runs, but his glances back at shadows point to fear, not fitness.
b.clue: Ask what Leo's actions in this setting suggest about his feelings.

draft.title: Character, setting and events together
card: A narrative is a story. Its characters are the people or creatures in it. Its setting is the time and place. Its events are what happens.
These three work together. A writer can use the setting or an event to show what a character is like.
A character's reaction to a storm or a sudden shock shows their traits, such as bravery, fear or kindness.
Example: a flood rises in the night. Kai wakes his little sister and carries her to the roof before he thinks of himself. This shows Kai is caring and brave.
draft.remember: Setting and events put a character under pressure, and how the character reacts shows what they are like.

a.q: Zara's boat is hit by a sudden wave. She grips the wheel, calls calm orders to her crew and steers on. What does this event show about Zara?
opts: She stays calm and leads under pressure
She is careless and ignores danger
She is shy and avoids other people
She is jealous of her crew
a.why: Zara's calm orders during a sudden wave show how she acts under pressure, so the event reveals her as calm and a leader. Careless is tempting because she steers on, but she is giving orders to keep the crew safe, not ignoring the danger.
a.clue: Look at what Zara does when the wave hits.

b.q: Leo hears thunder as he walks home through a dark, empty park. He runs the whole way, glancing back at every shadow. Which statement best explains how the writer reveals Leo's character?
opts: The stormy, dark setting leads Leo to show he is fearful
The thunder tells readers that Leo is a strong runner
The park shows that Leo is lonely and wants friends
Leo's running shows that he is in a hurry to eat dinner
b.why: The dark park and thunder form a setting that puts Leo under pressure, and his running and glancing back show he is fearful. The strong runner option is tempting because he runs, but the text gives his reason for running as fear, not fitness.
b.clue: Ask what Leo's actions in this setting suggest about his feelings.

version.title: Character, setting and events together
card: A narrative is a story. Its characters are the people or creatures in it. Its setting is the time and place. Its events are what happens.
These three work together. A writer can use the setting or an event to show what a character is like.
A storm or a sudden shock can put a character under pressure. How they react can show traits such as bravery, fear or kindness.

a.q: A sudden wave hits Zara's boat. She grips the wheel, tells each crew member what to do and keeps steering. What does her reaction to the wave reveal about her?
opts: She is calm and takes the lead
She is careless and ignores danger
She is shy and avoids her crew
She is jealous and blames her crew
a.why: The sudden wave puts Zara under pressure, and she responds by directing her crew and holding her course. That shows she stays steady and leads. Careless is tempting because she keeps steering, but she is acting to keep the crew safe, not ignoring the danger.
a.clue: How does Zara act in the moment the wave strikes?

b.q: Thunder rumbles as Leo crosses a dark, empty park on his way home. He races the whole way and keeps looking back at every shadow. How does the writer reveal what Leo is like?
opts: His reaction to the stormy setting shows he is fearful
The thunder tells readers that Leo is a strong runner
The empty park shows that Leo is lonely and wants friends
His racing shows he is in a hurry to get to his dinner
b.why: The writer never says Leo is afraid. Readers work it out from how he reacts to the dark, stormy park: he races and keeps looking back at shadows. The strong runner option is tempting because he runs, but looking back at shadows points to fear, not fitness.
b.clue: What do Leo's actions in this place suggest he is feeling?

a.best: She is calm and takes the lead

b.best: His reaction to the stormy setting shows he is fearful
